title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: The sheet is reused scrap paper. The bulk of it is an upside-down typescript page (p. 17) of a course on analytic functions over a complete valued field K; it is not Grothendieck's research text. Its content is as follows. (i) Cauchy-type estimates: if a convergent power series has sup-norm at most M on the polydisc boundary |z_i| = r_i, then ||c_{n_1...n_p}|| <= M / (r_1^{n_1} ... r_p^{n_p}). Hence the series M Π (x_i/r_i)^{n_i} majorises the given series; its sum is M / Π(1 - x_i/r_i). A second majorant is obtained by substituting u = Σ x_i/r_i into the geometric series M Σ u^n. Its coefficients are multinomial integers (>= 1) times M / r^n, and its sum is M / (1 - Σ x_i/r_i) near 0. (ii) §2, 'Résolution des équations analytiques', Théorème 1: the holomorphic implicit function theorem. If q holomorphic functions f_i(x; y) on an open A ⊂ K^{p+q} vanish at (a; b) and the Jacobian det(∂f_i/∂y_j) is nonzero there, then there are unique holomorphic u_i near a with u(a) = b and f(x, u(x)) = 0. Uniqueness holds among solutions continuous at a; the statement is cut off. The handwritten jottings by Grothendieck are unrelated to the typescript. They belong to the surrounding manuscript on Picard categories, Gr-categories, Ext-categories and torsor-categories (the 'catégorie de Picard de Breen' of the next page). They read: Z_p( ; Q(i) ; T ; B^o_c(Z) ; TORS( ; the Legendre symbol (-1/p) = -1 ; p ≡ 1 (4) ; '-1 carré mod p'. These are scratch reminders of the elementary fact that -1 is a square mod p iff p ≡ 1 mod 4, i.e. p splits in Q(i). Presumably Grothendieck was testing an example for the categories B_0 (here over Z, apparently with subscript c) and their torsor-categories. A plausible case is orders or bimodules attached to Q(i) and Z_p, distinguishing split and inert primes. The fragments are too sparse to reconstruct a specific statement.
errors: No mathematical errors in the typescript. The majorant M/(1 - Σ x_i/r_i) converges only for Σ|x_i|/r_i < 1; this is correctly described as 'a sufficiently small neighbourhood'.
The jotting '(-1/p) = -1' is correct exactly for p ≡ 3 mod 4. Next to it, 'p ≡ 1 (4)' is the case where -1 is a square; both cases are simply being recorded.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a reused sheet of a standard analysis typescript (majorants, implicit function theorem). Grothendieck's own marks are isolated scratch notations (Z_p, Q(i), Legendre symbol, TORS, B^o_c(Z)). Nothing substantive or unpublished can be read off.
transcription_corrections: Handwritten 'T' appears near top centre; top-left reads approximately '4 Z_p(' and 'Q(i)' with a superscript mark, possibly 'Q(i)*'.
Handwritten '(4)' sits under 'p ≡ 1', i.e. 'p ≡ 1 (4)'. 'd carré mod p' / '-1 carré mod p' is written small next to a large '-1'.
'B^o_c(Z)' may be 'B^0_C(Z)'. 'TORS(' is followed by an unclosed parenthesis.
Handwritten overstrokes near equation (1), '=0 (1≤i≤q)', are just retracings of the typescript.
